findings.mechanism: Static ConcurrentHashMap AWAITING gets an entry per charge in ChargeService.charge (line 26). The only removal is InFlightCharges.complete, called solely from ChargeListener.onPosted (line 20). ChargeListener.onRejected and onExpired never remove the entry, so every declined or expired charge keeps its PendingCharge (and ChargeRequest with email, invoice, account strings) reachable from the static map for the life of the JVM. Nothing else evicts or bounds the map.
findings.cause: Missing InFlightCharges.complete(ticket.id()) in the onRejected and onExpired callbacks (the ticket is passed to both). Fix: remove the entry in all terminal callbacks, e.g. in a finally or a shared helper, and/or add a TTL sweep using oldestAgeMillis.
findings.evidence: Code reading only. The proprietary internal.billing:ledger-client:3.2.1 dependency is not in the local Maven repo (only a .lastUpdated stub) and there is no network, so I could not build or run it, and I did not measure growth. Main prints the awaiting count after drain(); I expect it to stay above zero by the number of rejected or expired charges.
findings.discriminator: After ledger.drain(), service.inFlight() should be 0 if every charge reached a terminal state. A count that stays equal to the number of rejected plus expired charges, and a heap histogram showing PendingCharge and ChargeRequest instances held by InFlightCharges.AWAITING, confirm this leak.
